title: Data of the normalized realization adjunction insertion shift laws
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring and uniformizer, and a finite-field datum $D$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. Use the actual system and integral derived categories, reduction $\mathcal R$, total limit $\mathcal L$, and adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], an operation package $o$ and its realization package $c$ from [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization], and the actual inverse-unit and unary and tensor insertion maps of [lem-pur-integral-realization-recursion]. Use exactly the designated shift comparisons of [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data], including the signed second tensor slot and fixed total-limit comparison. Define the following predicate, not an assertion that it holds.

For functors $F,G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between categories with integer shifts, designated comparisons $\sigma_r(M):F(M[r])\cong F(M)[r]$ and $\tau_r(M):G(M[r])\cong G(M)[r]$, actual arrows $a_M:F(M)\to G(M)$, and an input predicate $P$, define $\operatorname{InsertionShiftLaw}(F,G,\sigma,\tau,a,P)$ to mean: (i) there is a $\operatorname{CommShift}$ structure on each of $F,G$ whose components are exactly $\sigma,\tau$ (so the fixed comparisons satisfy naturality and zero and addition coherence); (ii) for every $M$ satisfying $P$, $a_M$ is invertible and, for every $r\in\mathbf Z$, $\tau_r(M)\circ a_{M[r]}=a_M[r]\circ\sigma_r(M)$; (iii) for every $f:M\to N$ with $P(M)$ and $P(N)$, $a_N\circ F(f)=G(f)\circ a_M$. Define the composite designated comparison for $G\circ F$ by $\tau_r(FM)\circ G(\sigma_r(M))$. The source comparison for $\mathcal L A$ and target comparison for $A_{\rm int}\mathcal L$ are these composites in that order, using the fixed total-limit comparison.

Define $\operatorname{RealizationAdjunctionInsertionShift}(\ell,E,D,o,c)$ as the conjunction of six families of these laws: the inverse-unit law, the pullback insertion law, the proper-image insertion law, the quasi-compact open-extension insertion law, and the separate first-slot and second-slot tensor insertion laws. Quantify over all finite-type $k$-schemes, separated finite-type pullback maps, proper direct-image maps, and quasi-compact open immersions as appropriate, and over four arbitrary integer bounds $a,b,t_a,t_b$. For the inverse unit use $F=\mathcal L\mathcal R$, $G=\mathrm{id}$, the actual inverse-or-zero of the adjunction unit as $a$, the composite reduction/limit comparison and the identity target comparison; its input domain consists of the derived-complete constructible integral inputs of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] whose reduced systems are admissible with these bounds. For each unary operation $A$ use $F=\mathcal L A$, $G=A_{\rm int}\mathcal L$, its actual insertion $a_A$, and its input and output systems admissible with these same bounds. For tensor fix the other system operand, use the corresponding curried tensor functors and the actual $a_\otimes(M,N)$, and require both operands and their tensor output to be admissible with these bounds. Here admissibility is the normalization, compatible bounded-below etale-origin witnesses, constructibility and common finite cohomology and Tor bounds of [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain], with finite Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. All shifts range over every integer, and no choice of arbitrary insertion arrow or shift comparison is made.
